Correct classification: **Aurora kinase inhibitors** confirmed.

Evidence synthesis:
- Quantitative profile: frac_large_nucleus z up to +101 (0.31 vs 0.008 DMSO), nuc_area +42.6 to +44.9, nuc_dna_integrated ~2-2.5x, cell_area 2x, low solidity/form-factor (lobed/irregular) across 0.3-3 µM; no increase in frac_mitotic_like (rho 0) excluding Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest, intact tubulin/actin per microscopist.

reflection.text:
Compound AZ258 (PubChem CID 59396138, no curated ChEMBL mechanism, BBBC021 structure) unblinded as Aurora kinase inhibitors - verdict correct, protocol correct, my call correct (0.88). Reflection on what worked and what was difficult:

What the evidence got right and why:

The phenotype was unambiguous polyploidy, not a single-well artifact. I acquired 4 wells across 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM (e2-e5) within the 4-well budget (e1) and saw replicated extreme z-scores: frac_large_nucleus z=+80.7 at 0.3uM, +70.3 at 1uM, +101.4 at 3uM, with nuc_area z=+38.0 to +44.9 and nuc_major_axis z=+22.7 to +29.6. That magnitude and replication across 3 low-to-mid doses is classic for cytokinesis failure.

The comparison to the reference atlas (e6) anchored this: NSC vote 3/4 Aurora kinase inhibitors with per-well similarities 0.892 (0.3uM), 0.818 (1uM), 0.851 (3uM), k-neighbours 9/10 Aurora, 1/10 DNA damage. This supports linking Aurora B inhibition to polyploidization through mitotic failure PMID 39639371, consistent with the enlarged nuclei phenotype we measured.

Microscopist descriptions (e7 4 fields, e8 2 fields both density lower vs DMSO) listed Aurora as top candidate, with DNA replication/DNA damage only as overlapping alternatives in e7 and sole Aurora in e8, with reports of intact tubulin/actin. Combined with dose_response frac_mitotic_like rho=0.00 (p=1, e12) I correctly down-weighted Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors (e13: 0.01 and 0.005).

What misled or was ambiguous and why:

The 10uM well (e3: 203 cells vs 421 at 0.3uM, nuc_area +25.2, nuc_major_axis +13.5, act_glcm_contrast +11.4) was the sole dissent: 1-NN DNA damage similarity 0.571 vs 0.82-0.89 for Aurora. In isolation this could suggest DNA damage or toxicity, and dose_response trends were flat/non-significant - frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 (p0.6, e9), nuc_area rho=-0.40 (p0.6, e10), nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.40 (p0.6, e11) due to n=4. I initially sampled 1 and 10uM to detect dose-dependency; the drop in frac_large_nucleus at 10uM prompted the intermediate 3uM acquisition (e5) which resolved it as saturation then cell loss at high dose, not a true reversal. The review critique is right: nuclear enlargement, DNA gain and binucleation persist at 10uM despite lower large-nucleus fraction, and the lower similarity 0.57 should be weighted less than the 3 high-similarity Aurora votes.

Acquisition choices: starting with mid/high doses was efficient to discriminate MoA, but I lacked a very low dose (e.g. 0.01-0.1uM) to define the onset threshold for polyploidy. Budget was exhausted after 4 wells, so phenotype descriptions and dose_response analyses were the only affordable steps - correctly no further acquisition would have changed the 3/4 majority vote.

Calibration: 0.88 leaving 0.05 DNA damage and 0.04 DNA replication (e13) was appropriate to the non-unanimous vote and to known overlap of enlarged nuclei phenotypes, rather than claiming 1.0. The submitted rationale and next experiment (pHH3-Ser10 IF and >4N flow cytometry vs reference Aurora compound) remain the correct confirmatory path in a real lab. No clinical inference is warranted from screening morphology alone.
